\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{જુગાર} (jugār)}{જુગાર (jugār)}]{\gu{જુગાર} (jugār) — gambling}

\label{lesson:GU-C534-jugar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a round (of a game), then the Gujarati for to play a game of chance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{જુગાર}}
\textbf{\gu{જુગાર}} — \emph{jugār} — \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તું} \gu{જુગાર} \gu{રમીશ} \gu{તો} \gu{બધા} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{ગુમાવીશ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tũ jugār ramīś to badhā paisā gumāvīś.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you gamble, you will lose all your money.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{જુગાર}} (\emph{jugār}) is usually traced to Sanskrit \emph{dyūtakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}a gambler\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{dyūta}, \textquotedblleft{}gambling\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6609); CDIAL itself lists no Gujarati form there.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jugār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jugār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tũ jugār ramīś to badhā paisā gumāvīś.} — If you gamble, you will lose all your money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a round (of a game), then the Gujarati for to play a game of chance, then say \emph{jugār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{જુગાર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Gambling\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સટ્ટો} (saṭṭo)}{સટ્ટો (saṭṭo)}]{\gu{સટ્ટો} (saṭṭo) — a speculative bet}

\label{lesson:GU-C534-satto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to play a game of chance, then the Gujarati for gambling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સટ્ટો}}
\textbf{\gu{સટ્ટો}} — \emph{saṭṭo} — \textquotedblleft{}a speculative bet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{સટ્ટામાં} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{નાખશો} \gu{તો} \gu{કદાચ} \gu{બધું} \gu{જશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame saṭṭāmā̃ paisā nākhśo to kadāc badhũ jaśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you put money into speculation, you may lose it all.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સટ્ટો}} (\emph{saṭṭo}) is a bet on prices or results. CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{sāṭũ}, \textquotedblleft{}a bargain\textquotedblright{}, and Panjabi \emph{saṭṭī}, \textquotedblleft{}an exchange market\textquotedblright{}, under a reconstructed \emph{*saṭṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}exchange\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13101); it does not list this word, so its history is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṭṭo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṭṭo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame saṭṭāmā̃ paisā nākhśo to kadāc badhũ jaśe.} — If you put money into speculation, you may lose it all.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to play a game of chance, then the Gujarati for gambling, then say \emph{saṭṭo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{સટ્ટો} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A speculative bet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{હોડ} (hoḍ)}{હોડ (hoḍ)}]{\gu{હોડ} (hoḍ) — a wager}

\label{lesson:GU-C534-hod}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for gambling, then the Gujarati for a speculative bet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{હોડ}}
\textbf{\gu{હોડ}} — \emph{hoḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}a wager\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{આજે} \gu{વરસાદ} \gu{પડશે} \gu{તો} \gu{હું} \gu{હોડ} \gu{હારી} \gu{જઈશ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo āje varsād paḍśe to hũ hoḍ hārī jaīś.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains today, I'll lose the bet.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{હોડ}} (\emph{hoḍ}) comes from \emph{*hōḍḍa}, a form CDIAL reconstructs, and CDIAL lists the Gujarati word, \textquotedblleft{}a wager\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 14175).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo āje varsād paḍśe to hũ hoḍ hārī jaīś.} — If it rains today, I'll lose the bet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for gambling, then the Gujarati for a speculative bet, then say \emph{hoḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{હોડ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wager\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{લોટરી} (loṭrī)}{લોટરી (loṭrī)}]{\gu{લોટરી} (loṭrī) — a lottery}

\label{lesson:GU-C534-lotri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a speculative bet, then the Gujarati for a wager.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{લોટરી}}
\textbf{\gu{લોટરી}} — \emph{loṭrī} — \textquotedblleft{}a lottery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{મને} \gu{લોટરી} \gu{લાગશે} \gu{તો} \gu{હું} \gu{મારી} \gu{માતા} \gu{માટે} \gu{નવું} \gu{ઘર} \gu{ખરીદીશ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo mane loṭrī lāgśe to hũ mārī mātā māṭe navũ ghar kharīdīś.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I win the lottery, I'll buy a new house for my mother.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{લોટરી}} (\emph{loṭrī}) is borrowed from English \emph{lottery}. A lottery \textquotedblleft{}strikes\textquotedblright{} the winner: \textbf{\gu{મને} \gu{લોટરી} \gu{લાગી}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{loṭrī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{loṭrī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo mane loṭrī lāgśe to hũ mārī mātā māṭe navũ ghar kharīdīś.} — If I win the lottery, I'll buy a new house for my mother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a speculative bet, then the Gujarati for a wager, then say \emph{loṭrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{લોટરી} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lottery\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{જોગાનુજોગ} (jogānujog)}{જોગાનુજોગ (jogānujog)}]{\gu{જોગાનુજોગ} (jogānujog) — a chance meeting; a coincidence}

\label{lesson:GU-C534-joganujog}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a wager, then the Gujarati for a lottery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{જોગાનુજોગ}}
\textbf{\gu{જોગાનુજોગ}} — \emph{jogānujog} — \textquotedblleft{}a chance meeting; a coincidence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{હું} \gu{મોડો} \gu{આવત} \gu{તો} \gu{આ} \gu{જોગાનુજોગ} \gu{ન} \gu{બનત}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo hũ moḍo āvat to ā jogānujog na banat.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I had come late, this coincidence would never have happened.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{જોગાનુજોગ}} (\emph{jogānujog}) is built from \emph{jog}, \textquotedblleft{}a meeting, a joining\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{yoga}, \textquotedblleft{}joining\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with \emph{anu}, \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}: one meeting falling after another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogānujog}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogānujog}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo hũ moḍo āvat to ā jogānujog na banat.} — If I had come late, this coincidence would never have happened.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a wager, then the Gujarati for a lottery, then say \emph{jogānujog} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{જોગાનુજોગ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A chance meeting; a coincidence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
